page.overview:
Who is Peter Jackson?

Sir Peter Jackson (born October 31, 1961 in Pukerua Bay, Porirua City, New Zealand) is a New Zealander film writer, director, and producer. He directed, produced, and helped to adapt both the live-action film trilogies for and , which are based on J.R.R. Tolkien's novels, trilogy and , respectively.

Jackson's first public showings in cinema were "splatstick" horror comedy Bad Taste (1987), the black comedy Meet the Feebles (1989), and gore comedy Braindead (1992; also known as Dead Alive), but he later pivoted to more dramatic works such as the movie Heavenly Creatures (1994), for which he shared with Fran Walsh an Oscar nomination for "Best Screenplay Written Directly for the Screen". He did return to his horror comedy roots with The Frighteners (1996)

He reached fame later, with his direction of the epic film trilogy The Lord of the Rings (2001 - 2003), based on the books of the same name by J.R.R. Tolkien. The of the trilogy earned an Oscar in all 11 categories it was nominated for. In 2012, Jackson remastered the trilogy as a brand new digital transfer from the original source, which was the Blu Ray release. Also beginning in 2012, the of what would be the The Hobbit trilogy of films premier with the remaining two premiering in 2013 and 2014 respectively.

Between the two trilogies, he directed King Kong (2005) and The Lovely Bones (2005), as well as producing the sci-fi film District 9. After the The Hobbit trilogy, he worked on the screenplay and helped produce Mortal Engines (2018).
